Vance’s office said it contacted the Democrat after hearing he wanted to talk, The Hill reported on Friday.
The Vice President’s Office and El-Sayed’s Office did not immediately respond to
request for comments.
Vance Signals Openness After Midterm Fallout
The development follows Vance telling Fox News’ “The Ingraham Angle” on Monday that El-Sayed would find the White House “a willing partner” if he wants to work with the administration.
In response, El-Sayed replied on X, tagging Vance. “For me, it will always be about serving working people,” he wrote. He said he is looking forward to the conversation.
